name: Orion Nebula
notes: Nearest massive star-forming region; lit by the Trapezium cluster.

name: De Mairan's Nebula
notes: H II region around NU Ori; part of the Orion Nebula complex.

name: Flame Nebula
notes: Ionised by Alnitak's neighbourhood; embedded young cluster.

name: Horsehead Nebula
notes: Dark pillar silhouetted against the emission nebula IC 434.

name: M78
notes: Brightest reflection nebula in the sky.

name: NGC 1999
notes: Lit by the young star V380 Ori.

name: Barnard's Loop
notes: Huge arc of ionised gas blown out by the Orion OB1 association.

name: Lambda Orionis Ring
notes: Ring of gas and dust around the Lambda Ori cluster.

name: Witch Head Nebula
notes: Lit by Rigel.

name: Gum Nebula
notes: Ancient supernova remnant / H II region about 36° across, one of the largest nebulae in the sky.

name: Trifid Nebula
notes: Emission + reflection + dark lanes in one object.

name: Eagle Nebula
notes: Home of the Pillars of Creation.

name: Omega Nebula
notes: Also called the Swan Nebula.

name: Rosette Nebula
notes: Shell carved by the cluster NGC 2244.

name: Hubble's Variable Nebula
notes: Fan-shaped nebula lit by R Monocerotis; varies over weeks.

name: Thor's Helmet
notes: Wind-blown bubble around the Wolf-Rayet star WR 7.

name: Pelican Nebula
notes: Part of the same H II region as the North America Nebula.

name: Crescent Nebula
notes: Wind-blown shell around the Wolf-Rayet star WR 136.

name: Bubble Nebula
notes: Bubble blown by the O star BD+60° 2522.

name: Ghost of Cassiopeia
notes: Lit and eroded by Gamma Cassiopeiae.

name: California Nebula
notes: Ionised by the runaway O star Xi Persei.

name: NGC 1333
notes: Young embedded cluster in the Perseus molecular cloud.

name: Flaming Star Nebula
notes: Lit by the runaway star AE Aurigae.

name: Hind's Variable Nebula
notes: Lit by T Tauri.

name: Pleiades Nebula
notes: Dust cloud the Pleiades are passing through (Merope Nebula).

name: Rho Ophiuchi Nebula
notes: Closest star-forming region to the Sun with multicoloured nebulosity.

name: Antares Nebula
notes: Yellow reflection nebula around Antares.

name: Blue Horsehead Nebula
notes: Lit by Nu Scorpii.

name: Chamaeleon Nebula
notes: Brightest nebula of the Chamaeleon I cloud.

name: Carina Nebula
notes: Home of Eta Carinae; one of the brightest H II regions in the Galaxy.

name: Running Chicken Nebula
notes: Contains Thackeray's dark globules.

name: Helix Nebula
notes: One of the closest bright planetary nebulae.

name: Southern Ring Nebula
notes: Imaged by JWST in 2022.

name: Bug Nebula
notes: Butterfly-shaped; one of the hottest known central stars.

name: Sh2-216
notes: Nearest known planetary nebula; very old and faint.

name: Crab Nebula
notes: Remnant of the supernova of 1054 AD, powered by the Crab pulsar.

name: Veil Nebula / Cygnus Loop
notes: Supernova remnant about 10–20 thousand years old.

name: Vela Supernova Remnant
notes: About 11,000 years old; contains the Vela pulsar.

name: Cassiopeia A
notes: Youngest known Galactic core-collapse remnant (about 1680 AD).

name: Tycho's Supernova Remnant
notes: Remnant of the Type Ia supernova seen by Tycho Brahe in 1572.

name: Kepler's Supernova Remnant
notes: Last supernova seen in the Milky Way with the naked eye (1604).

name: SN 1006
notes: Brightest supernova in recorded history.

name: Manatee Nebula
notes: Supernova remnant distorted by the jets of the microquasar SS 433.

name: Coalsack Nebula
notes: The most prominent dark nebula visible to the naked eye.

name: Barnard 68
notes: Isolated dense core (Bok globule) on the verge of collapse.

name: Dark Doodad
notes: Long thin filament of dust in Musca.
